boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all ten frozen records in the Gettysburg Campaign [June-July 1863]. Preserve per-engagement dates. Middleburg (June 17–19) overlaps Aldie (June 17), and Boonsboro (July 8) lies inside Williamsport's frozen interval (July 6–16); campaign-wide and multi-day totals (for example Stuart's June 17–21 losses and the Count of Paris's campaign estimates) must not be assigned to one engagement or added. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

Doubleday relays the Confederate claim that they fell back only on Stuart's orders and judges the loss of the pass a serious blow to the Confederates.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Doubleday's 'serious blow' is his judgment and campaign context.

open_questions: Kilpatrick's, Gregg's, Munford's and Fitz Lee's reports and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Doubleday is an interested participant history (he commanded the First Corps at Gettysburg) and Humphreys an interested history by Meade's later chief of staff; both drew on official papers. Lee's and Stuart's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXVII, Part 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
